sections.text:
In one of the ancient and rich Arab cities in the Middle East, a poor young man named "Aladdin" lived with his widowed mother.

Aladdin did not have a job, and he spent his days running in the markets and crowded alleys, dreaming of the day when he would become rich to comfort his mother.

One day, a strange man came claiming to be his uncle (his deceased father's brother), and this man was in fact an evil sorcerer from a distant land.

The magician gave Aladdin new clothes and money to trick him, then took him on a long journey into the desert, where they stopped in front of a huge rock.

The magician muttered magic words, and the earth split open and a secret door appeared leading to a deep underground cave called the “Cave of Wonders.”

The magician said to Aladdin: “Go down to the cave, my son. You will find great treasures. Take whatever you want from them, but there is an old copper lamp. Bring it to me and do not touch anything else!”

The magician gave Aladdin a magic ring to protect him from dangers, and the astonished young man descended into the depths of the cave, where he saw mountains of gold and precious gems.

Aladdin could not resist the temptation of jewels, so he filled his pockets with them, then found the old lamp and took it as he was asked.

When he reached the exit of the cave, the magician asked him to give him the lamp first before helping him out, but Aladdin doubted his intention and refused to hand it over.

The magician became very angry and closed the cave door forcefully, leaving Aladdin trapped in complete darkness underground.

Aladdin sat crying, and accidentally rubbed the magic ring that the magician had given him, and a small genie came out of it and helped him get out of the cave.

Aladdin returned to his mother carrying the jewels and the old copper lamp, which looked dirty, so his mother decided to clean it to sell it in the market.

As soon as I started rubbing the lamp with a cloth, it shook violently and thick blue smoke came out of it, taking the form of a very giant genie!
The giant said in a loud voice: “What do you do to me? Your servant is in your hands. I am the genie of the lamp. What do you command, sir? Ask whatever you want!”

The mother was terrified, but Aladdin took courage and said confidently: “I am very hungry. I want a table full of the most delicious food!”

In one second, a golden table appeared in front of them carrying plates of the most delicious meats, sweets, and fruits.

Thanks to the magic lamp, the lives of Aladdin and his mother changed, and they became among the wealthy people of the city after they sold the golden dishes and bought a small palace.

One day, while Aladdin was in the market, he saw Princess Jasmine, the Sultan's daughter, walking around incognito to escape the boredom of the palace.

He was enchanted by her beauty, and when he discovered her identity, he decided to propose to her. He asked the genie to provide him with the finest clothes and a great procession loaded with boxes of jewels to present to the Sultan.

The Sultan was impressed by Aladdin's gift, and agreed to marry Princess Jasmine, especially after the genie built her a wonderful palace of gold and marble in one night.

Aladdin and Jasmine lived very happily, until the evil magician heard the news of the rich young man and his strange palace, and he realized that Aladdin had survived and that the lamp was in his possession.

The magician traveled to the city and disguised himself as a peddler calling out in the streets: “I replace old lamps with new, shiny lamps!”

Princess Jasmine's maid heard the call, and because she did not know the secret of the old brass lamp in Aladdin's room, she took it and replaced it with a new one.

As soon as the magician got the lamp, he rubbed it and ordered the genie to transport the palace and the princess to a very distant country in Africa.

Aladdin returned and did not find his palace or his wife. He was very sad, but he remembered the magic ring that was still on his finger!
He rubbed the ring and asked the ring genie to take it to the location of the princess's palace.

Aladdin arrived at the palace, infiltrated it, and devised a clever plan with Yasmine to get rid of the magician.

Jasmine put a sleeping pill in the magician's drink during dinner, and when he fell into a deep sleep, Aladdin took the lamp and rubbed it immediately.

Aladdin ordered the genie of the lamp to send the evil magician to a far away place from which he would never return, and to return the palace and the princess to their city.

The wish was fulfilled, and the palace returned to its place amid the joy of the Sultan and the people of the city.

Aladdin and Princess Jasmine lived in safety and peace, and Aladdin learned that intelligence and courage were much more important than magic and wealth.
